topics.name: Sorting Algorithm Race
topics.concept: Different sorting algorithms trade comparisons, swaps, and memory in ways that only show up on real data. This tool runs bubble, insertion, merge, quick, and heap sort on the same seeded arrays, counting comparisons and swaps and timing each. Watching quicksort's partitions against merge sort's steady halves builds lasting intuition.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates arrays in several orderings for fair comparison.
topics.real_world_use: Used in CS courses and interviews to teach algorithm tradeoffs.

topics.name: Quicksort Partition Visualizer
topics.concept: Quicksort's speed comes from partitioning: picking a pivot and shuffling smaller elements left and larger right, then recursing. The visualizer steps through partition schemes like Lomuto and Hoare on a bar display, highlighting the pivot, the scanning pointers, and the swaps. Bad pivot choices visibly degrade into quadratic behavior.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds arrays that expose best and worst-case pivot behavior.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching divide-and-conquer sorting.

topics.name: Merge Sort Trace
topics.concept: Merge sort guarantees n log n time by splitting arrays down to single elements and merging the sorted halves back together. The tracer shows the recursion tree, the split phases, and each merge step with its comparisons. Its stability and predictability become obvious next to quicksort's variance.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates arrays for split-and-merge tracing.
topics.real_world_use: Used in algorithms courses demonstrating guaranteed performance.

topics.name: Heap Sort Heapify Demo
topics.concept: Heap sort turns the array into a max-heap, then repeatedly extracts the maximum to the end. The demo visualizes the array as a binary tree, showing sift-down operations restoring the heap property after each extraction. It connects the abstract heap to the concrete array indices.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates arrays needing varied heapify work.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching heaps through sorting.

topics.name: Radix Sort Digit Passes
topics.concept: Radix sort skips comparisons entirely, sorting integers digit by digit with stable counting sort passes. The tool shows each pass grouping numbers by the current digit, demonstrating why the least-significant-digit-first order works. Linear time on fixed-width keys feels like magic until you see the passes.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates fixed-width integers for digit passes.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching non-comparative sorting.

topics.name: Binary Search Trainer
topics.concept: Binary search halves a sorted array each step, finding any element in logarithmic time, but off-by-one errors plague implementations. The trainer lets users guess the midpoint sequence, checks each step, and explains the invariant that the target stays within the bounds. It drills the pattern until it is automatic.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds sorted arrays and picks targets including missing values.
topics.real_world_use: Used in interview prep for search fundamentals.

topics.name: Interpolation Search Demo
topics.concept: When data is uniformly distributed, interpolation search guesses position by value proportion instead of blindly halving, often beating binary search. The demo compares probe counts of both strategies on uniform versus skewed data. It shows how distributional knowledge buys speed.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates uniform and clustered value distributions.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching adaptive search strategies.

topics.name: Linked List Playground
topics.concept: Linked lists chain nodes through pointers, trading cache-unfriendly traversal for O(1) insertion at known positions. The playground supports insert, delete, reverse, and cycle creation with step-by-step pointer visualization. Seeing the pointers move demystifies the structure.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds lists and operation scripts including cycles.
topics.real_world_use: Used in data-structures courses.

topics.name: Hash Table Collision Lab
topics.concept: Hash tables map keys to buckets in average constant time, but collisions are inevitable and the resolution strategy defines performance. The lab inserts keys under chaining and open addressing with linear, quadratic, and double hashing, measuring probe lengths as load factor grows. The load-factor cliff becomes visceral.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates keys with controllable hash clustering.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching hashing and collision resolution.

topics.name: BST Operation Visualizer
topics.concept: Binary search trees keep left subtrees smaller and right subtrees larger than each node, giving logarithmic search when balanced. The visualizer inserts, deletes, and searches with rotations of the tree drawn after each step. Degenerate insertion order visibly collapses it into a linked list.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates insertion orders from random to adversarial.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching tree invariants.

topics.name: AVL Rotation Demo
topics.concept: AVL trees rebalance after every update so heights of child subtrees differ by at most one, guaranteeing logarithmic operations. The demo triggers each rotation case, single and double, left and right, showing the before and after shapes with balance factors. Self-balancing stops being abstract.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG crafts insertion orders hitting all four rotation cases.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching self-balancing trees.

topics.name: Trie Autocomplete Engine
topics.concept: Tries store strings character by character in a tree, making prefix searches and autocomplete naturally efficient. The engine builds a trie from a word list, serves prefix completions ranked by frequency, and visualizes the shared prefixes. It is the data structure behind every search box.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates vocabularies with word frequencies.
topics.real_world_use: Used in search boxes and spell checkers.

topics.name: Segment Tree Range Queries
topics.concept: Range sum or minimum queries over arrays are slow if recomputed, so segment trees precompute interval aggregates in a tree for logarithmic queries and updates. The tool builds the tree, answers range queries showing visited nodes, and applies point updates. It unlocks a whole class of range problems.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates arrays with query and update workloads.
topics.real_world_use: Used in competitive programming for range problems.

topics.name: Fenwick Tree Demo
topics.concept: Fenwick trees answer prefix sums with less code and memory than segment trees, using clever bit manipulation on indices. The demo shows the internal tree array, how lowbit jumps traverse it, and compares operation counts against naive prefix sums. Elegance through bit tricks.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates arrays with update and query mixes.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching compact range-sum structures.

topics.name: Union-Find Connectivity
topics.concept: Union-find tracks which elements share a set with near-constant amortized time using path compression and union by rank. The tool processes union and find operations on a grid, visualizing component merges for percolation-style problems. It powers Kruskal's algorithm and dynamic connectivity.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates union operations with cluster structure.
topics.real_world_use: Used in network connectivity and Kruskal's MST.

topics.name: Bloom Filter Lab
topics.concept: Bloom filters answer set membership with a tiny bit array and a tunable false-positive rate, never false negatives. The lab inserts items, tests membership, and measures the actual false-positive rate against the theoretical formula as parameters change. It shows probabilistic data structures earning their keep.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates inserted and queried item sets.
topics.real_world_use: Used in databases and caches to skip disk lookups.

topics.name: LRU Cache Simulator
topics.concept: LRU caches evict the least recently used entry, implemented with a hash map plus doubly linked list for O(1) operations. The simulator runs get and put sequences showing hits, misses, and evictions with the recency order visible. Cache behavior becomes predictable.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates access patterns from locality-heavy to scans.
topics.real_world_use: Used in web caches and database buffer pools.

topics.name: LFU Cache Simulator
topics.concept: LFU evicts the least frequently used entry, beating LRU when popularity is stable but suffering when it shifts. The simulator compares hit rates of LRU, LFU, and FIFO across workloads, showing where each policy wins. Policy choice becomes data-driven.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG creates workloads with stable and shifting popularity.
topics.real_world_use: Used tuning cache policies for CDNs and databases.

topics.name: Min-Heap Priority Queue
topics.concept: Priority queues serve the smallest or largest item first, and binary heaps deliver logarithmic push and pop. The tool visualizes the heap array as a tree through pushes, pops, and priority updates. It is the engine inside Dijkstra and task schedulers.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates priority workloads.
topics.real_world_use: Used in schedulers and graph algorithms.

topics.name: BFS DFS Maze Explorer
topics.concept: Breadth-first search explores level by level finding shortest paths in unweighted graphs, while depth-first dives deep using less memory. The explorer runs both on generated mazes, animating the frontier and visited sets side by side. Their different personalities become obvious.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates solvable mazes with start and goal.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching graph traversal.

topics.name: Dijkstra Pathfinder
topics.concept: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths from a source by always expanding the closest unvisited node, which works when edge weights are non-negative. The pathfinder animates the priority queue and distance labels on weighted grids and graphs. It is the foundation of routing.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds weighted graphs with varied edge costs.
topics.real_world_use: Used in GPS routing and network path computation.

topics.name: A-Star Grid Navigator
topics.concept: A-star guides Dijkstra with a heuristic estimating remaining distance, exploring far fewer nodes when the heuristic is admissible. The navigator compares node expansions of Dijkstra, greedy, and A-star on obstacle grids with Manhattan and Euclidean heuristics. Good heuristics feel like cheating.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates obstacle maps with guaranteed paths.
topics.real_world_use: Used in game AI and robotics pathfinding.

topics.name: Bellman-Ford Demo
topics.concept: Bellman-Ford handles negative edge weights that break Dijkstra, relaxing all edges repeatedly and detecting negative cycles on the final pass. The demo traces relaxation rounds on graphs with negative edges, showing distance labels converging. It trades speed for generality.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds graphs with negative edges, some with cycles.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching shortest paths with negative weights.

topics.name: Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs
topics.concept: Floyd-Warshall computes shortest paths between every pair of nodes with a triple loop that is beautifully simple. The tool shows the distance matrix evolving as intermediate nodes are allowed, which also reveals the dynamic programming structure. Cubic time buys complete answers.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates dense and sparse weighted graphs.
topics.real_world_use: Used for all-pairs routing tables.

topics.name: Kruskal MST Builder
topics.concept: Kruskal builds a minimum spanning tree by adding the cheapest edges that do not form cycles, using union-find for the cycle test. The builder sorts edges and shows each accept or reject decision with the growing forest. Greedy works here because of the matroid structure.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates weighted graphs for MST construction.
topics.real_world_use: Used in network design minimizing cable cost.

topics.name: Prim MST Grower
topics.concept: Prim grows the minimum spanning tree outward from a start node, always attaching the cheapest edge to the growing tree. The grower animates the frontier of candidate edges with a priority queue. Same optimal result as Kruskal through a different greedy lens.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds weighted graphs for tree growth.
topics.real_world_use: Used in clustering and network layout.

topics.name: Topological Sort Scheduler
topics.concept: Tasks with prerequisites form a directed acyclic graph, and topological order gives a valid execution sequence. The scheduler runs Kahn's algorithm on course-like dependencies, detects cycles that make scheduling impossible, and shows parallel levels. It is the algorithm behind build systems.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates DAGs with layered dependencies.
topics.real_world_use: Used in build tools and course planners.

topics.name: Kosaraju SCC Finder
topics.concept: Strongly connected components are groups where every node reaches every other, found by Kosaraju's two-pass DFS on the graph and its transpose. The finder colors components on directed graphs, showing the condensation DAG. It reveals the hidden modular structure of directed networks.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds directed graphs with clustered components.
topics.real_world_use: Used analyzing web graphs and dependency cycles.

topics.name: Cycle Detection Lab
topics.concept: Cycles in directed graphs mean circular dependencies, and detecting them early prevents deadlocks and infinite loops. The lab compares DFS coloring, Kahn's algorithm, and union-find approaches on graphs with and without cycles. Each method's trace teaches a different way to see the loop.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates graphs with and without planted cycles.
topics.real_world_use: Used in dependency analysis and deadlock detection.

topics.name: Max Flow Ford-Fulkerson
topics.concept: Maximum flow pushes the most units from source to sink through capacitated edges, with min-cut duality certifying optimality. The tool animates augmenting paths and residual graph updates on flow networks. It models everything from traffic to bipartite matching.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds flow networks with varied bottlenecks.
topics.real_world_use: Used in logistics and network throughput planning.

topics.name: Bipartite Matching Demo
topics.concept: Matching workers to jobs or students to projects is a bipartite matching problem, solved by augmenting paths or reduced to max flow. The demo matches two sets showing each augmenting assignment. It is the algorithm behind assignment problems everywhere.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates bipartite qualification graphs.
topics.real_world_use: Used in scheduling and resource allocation.

topics.name: Knapsack Solver
topics.concept: The 0/1 knapsack picks items maximizing value under a weight limit, solved exactly by dynamic programming over capacity. The solver builds the DP table showing how each item updates the best achievable value, then backtracks the chosen set. It is the canonical DP introduction.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates items with weights and values.
topics.real_world_use: Used in resource allocation and cargo loading.

topics.name: LCS Diff Engine
topics.concept: Longest common subsequence powers diff tools: the LCS of two texts is what stayed the same, and the rest are insertions and deletions. The engine computes the DP table and renders a unified diff from the backtrack. Every git diff runs on this idea.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG mutates base texts with edits to diff.
topics.real_world_use: Used in version control and plagiarism detection.

topics.name: Edit Distance Calculator
topics.concept: Edit distance counts the insertions, deletions, and substitutions turning one string into another, the basis of spell checking. The calculator fills the DP table and backtracks the optimal edit script. Close matches surface with their transformation shown.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG picks word pairs with typo-like differences.
topics.real_world_use: Used in spell checkers and DNA alignment.

topics.name: Coin Change Counter
topics.concept: Counting ways to make change and finding the minimum coins are classic DP problems with subtly different recurrences. The tool solves both variants, showing how the table differs between counting combinations and optimizing. Small change, deep lessons.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG picks amounts and denomination sets.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching DP formulation differences.

topics.name: LIS Finder
topics.concept: The longest increasing subsequence finds the longest sorted-across-gaps pattern, solvable in n log n with patience sorting. The finder shows both the quadratic DP and the piles method, revealing the elegant greedy insight. It appears in scheduling and bioinformatics.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates sequences with hidden long runs.
topics.real_world_use: Used in pattern analysis.

topics.name: Matrix Chain Optimizer
topics.concept: Multiplying a chain of matrices costs wildly different amounts depending on parenthesization, and DP finds the cheapest order. The optimizer computes the cost table and reconstructs the optimal parenthesization. It demonstrates DP over intervals.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates dimension chains with deceptive costs.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching interval dynamic programming.

topics.name: Subset Sum Explorer
topics.concept: Subset sum asks whether any subset hits a target, the decision problem behind knapsack and partition. The explorer builds the reachable-sums DP table and backtracks a witness subset when one exists. It introduces NP-completeness gently.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG crafts sets with and without solutions.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching NP-complete decision problems.

topics.name: Word Break Segmenter
topics.concept: Splitting a concatenated string into dictionary words is DP over prefixes with a trie for speed. The segmenter shows the DP array filling and reconstructs all valid segmentations. It is the algorithm behind hashtag splitting.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG concatenates dictionary words into test strings.
topics.real_world_use: Used in text segmentation and autocomplete.

topics.name: KMP Pattern Matcher
topics.concept: Knuth-Morris-Pratt skips ahead on mismatches using a prefix function, achieving linear-time search without backtracking. The matcher shows the prefix table construction and the text scan with its clever shifts. It turns string matching from quadratic to linear.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates texts with repetitive patterns stressing naive search.
topics.real_world_use: Used in text editors and intrusion detection.

topics.name: Rabin-Karp Rolling Hash
topics.concept: Rabin-Karp hashes the pattern and slides a rolling hash across the text, verifying only on hash matches. The tool demonstrates the rolling update arithmetic and shows how hash collisions are handled by verification. It shines for multi-pattern search.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds texts embedding the patterns.
topics.real_world_use: Used in plagiarism detection and multi-pattern scanning.

topics.name: Z-Algorithm Demo
topics.concept: The Z-algorithm computes for each position the longest prefix match in linear time, elegantly solving pattern matching. The demo fills the Z-array showing how the Z-box window reuses previous work. It is stringology's neat trick.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates strings with periodic structure.
topics.real_world_use: Used in string algorithms courses.

topics.name: Tower of Hanoi Solver
topics.concept: The Tower of Hanoi's recursive solution moves n-1 disks out of the way, moves the largest, then moves the stack again, taking 2^n minus 1 moves. The solver animates the optimal moves and proves minimality by the recurrence. Recursion's hello world.
topics.data_idea: The puzzle state is generated deterministically from disk count.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching recursion.

topics.name: N-Queens Solver
topics.concept: Placing n queens so none attack each other is the classic backtracking problem, with pruning cutting the search dramatically. The solver animates placements and backtracks, counting solutions for each n. Constraint propagation in miniature.
topics.data_idea: Board states derive from n; symmetry used for counting.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching backtracking and pruning.

topics.name: Sudoku Solver
topics.concept: Sudoku solving combines constraint propagation with backtracking search, trying candidates where forced. The solver shows candidate elimination and the search tree on hard puzzles. It is constraint satisfaction made tangible.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates puzzles with unique solutions.
topics.real_world_use: Used in puzzle apps and AI search courses.

topics.name: Maze Generator Solver
topics.concept: Perfect mazes come from randomized DFS carving or Prim's algorithm, and each generator has a visual texture. The tool generates mazes with several algorithms then solves them, comparing path lengths and dead ends. Generation and search in one playground.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG drives maze carving algorithms.
topics.real_world_use: Used in game level prototyping.

topics.name: Activity Selection Scheduler
topics.concept: Picking the maximum number of non-overlapping activities is solved greedily by earliest finish time, and the proof is instructive. The scheduler shows the greedy picks versus brute force on small inputs. The rare case where greedy is provably optimal.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates activity intervals.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching greedy correctness.

topics.name: Huffman Coding Compressor
topics.concept: Huffman coding assigns shorter bit codes to frequent symbols using a greedy tree merge, achieving optimal prefix-free compression. The tool builds the tree from symbol frequencies, shows the code table, and compresses sample text with ratio stats. Information theory you can watch.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates text with skewed symbol frequencies.
topics.real_world_use: Used in file compression like gzip and JPEG.

topics.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
topics.concept: The sieve finds all primes up to n by crossing out multiples, running in n log log n time. The visualizer animates the crossing-out passes and compares against trial division. Ancient algorithm, enduring elegance.
topics.data_idea: Prime ranges derive deterministically from the limit.
topics.real_world_use: Used in cryptography prime generation.

topics.name: Modular Exponentiation Lab
topics.concept: Fast modular exponentiation squares and multiplies in logarithmic time, making RSA-sized powers feasible. The lab traces the square-and-multiply steps and shows why naive multiplication is impossible at cryptographic sizes. The engine inside public-key crypto.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG picks bases and large exponents.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching the math behind RSA.

topics.name: Miller-Rabin Primality
topics.concept: Miller-Rabin tests primality probabilistically: composites are caught with probability 3/4 per round, so enough rounds mean practical certainty. The tool runs rounds on candidates showing witnesses, and compares against deterministic trial division. How crypto finds its primes.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates odd candidates including pseudoprimes.
topics.real_world_use: Used in cryptographic key generation.

topics.name: Fibonacci Fast Doubling
topics.concept: Fast doubling computes Fibonacci numbers in logarithmic time using identities that jump two steps at once, even for thousand-digit results. The tool compares naive recursion, memoization, iteration, and fast doubling on operation counts. A parable about algorithmic thinking.
topics.data_idea: Inputs are just the index n; outputs verified against known values.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching complexity classes.

topics.name: Convex Hull Finder
topics.concept: The convex hull wraps a point set in the smallest convex polygon, found by Graham scan sorting by angle or Jarvis march wrapping. The finder animates both on random point sets showing their different rhythms. Computational geometry's entry point.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG scatters points in the plane.
topics.real_world_use: Used in graphics and geographic analysis.

topics.name: Reservoir Sampling Demo
topics.concept: Reservoir sampling picks k uniform samples from a stream of unknown length in one pass, replacing entries with decreasing probability. The demo verifies uniformity statistically over many runs. Streaming algorithms start here.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG streams items for sampling trials.
topics.real_world_use: Used in stream processing and A/B testing.

topics.name: Skip List Demo
topics.concept: Skip lists layer express lanes over a linked list with random promotion, giving expected logarithmic search without rotations. The demo builds the tower structure and traces searches down the levels. Randomization replacing rebalancing.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG drives insertions with random level draws.
topics.real_world_use: Used in Redis sorted sets.

topics.name: Quickselect Demo
topics.concept: Quickselect finds the kth smallest element in expected linear time by partitioning like quicksort but recursing into only one side. The demo shows the discarded partitions and compares against full sorting. Selection without the sort.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates arrays for selection.
topics.real_world_use: Used in percentile and median computations.

topics.name: Consistent Hashing Ring
topics.concept: Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes onto a ring so adding a node moves only nearby keys, unlike naive modulo hashing. The visualizer places nodes and keys on the ring with virtual nodes, showing key migration on membership changes. The backbone of distributed caches.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG hashes keys and nodes onto the ring.
topics.real_world_use: Used in Dynamo, Cassandra, and memcached clients.

topics.name: Token Ring Simulator
topics.concept: Token passing grants exclusive access in a ring: only the holder may transmit, eliminating collisions deterministically. The simulator circulates the token showing wait times under varying loads. Old LANs ran on this idea.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates station traffic demands.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching deterministic medium access.

topics.name: Graph Coloring Scheduler
topics.concept: Scheduling exams or registers so conflicting items differ is graph coloring, NP-hard but greedy-friendly. The tool colors conflict graphs with greedy orderings showing how order affects color count. Approximation in action.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG builds conflict graphs.
topics.real_world_use: Used in register allocation and timetabling.

topics.name: Edit Script Compressor
topics.concept: Beyond computing edit distance, real diff tools compress the edit script into hunks humans can review. The tool generates diffs then groups nearby edits with context lines. From algorithm to usable tool.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG mutates texts producing edit clusters.
topics.real_world_use: Used in code review tooling.

topics.name: Suffix Array Builder
topics.concept: Suffix arrays sort all suffixes of a string enabling fast substring search and LCP queries. The builder shows the doubling construction sorting by 2^k prefixes. The index behind full-text search.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates strings with repeated substrings.
topics.real_world_use: Used in bioinformatics and text indexes.

topics.name: Closest Pair Sweep
topics.concept: Finding the closest pair among n points is O(n log n) with a sweep line, beating the quadratic check. The tool animates the sweep with its sliding strip of candidates. Divide and conquer in geometry.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG scatters points with a planted close pair.
topics.real_world_use: Used in graphics and collision detection.

topics.name: Boyer-Moore Matcher
topics.concept: Boyer-Moore scans the pattern from right to left and skips ahead using bad-character and good-suffix rules, often sublinear in practice. The matcher shows the skip tables and the jumps on natural-language text. The fastest practical single-pattern search.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates English-like text with pattern occurrences.
topics.real_world_use: Used in grep and text editors.

topics.name: Rod Cutting Optimizer
topics.concept: Cutting a rod into pieces to maximize revenue is the unbounded-knapsack-flavored DP classic. The optimizer fills the revenue table and reconstructs the optimal cut plan. Simple statement, rich structure.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates price tables with deceptive local optima.
topics.real_world_use: Used teaching DP over prefixes.

topics.name: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
topics.concept: The longest palindromic subsequence reveals the most symmetric hidden pattern, solved by DP over intervals. The tool fills the interval table and reconstructs the palindrome. A cousin of LCS with its own charm.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates strings with embedded palindromes.
topics.real_world_use: Used in sequence analysis.

topics.name: Egg Drop Puzzle
topics.concept: With two eggs and a 100-floor building, the optimal strategy balances worst-case drops via a clever DP, not binary search. The solver computes the optimal first drop and the decision tree. A puzzle that punishes naive halving.
topics.data_idea: Puzzle parameters derive deterministically from floors and eggs.
topics.real_world_use: Used in interview puzzles and DP teaching.

topics.name: Trapping Rain Water
topics.concept: Given elevation bars, trapped rainwater equals the sum over positions of min(left max, right max) minus height, computed in linear time with two pointers. The visualizer fills the water and shows the pointer sweep. A favorite interview problem made visual.
topics.data_idea: A seeded RNG generates elevation profiles with basins.
topics.real_world_use: Used in coding interview prep.
